_readme: Draft Nassington walk. [[c:...]] = cyan, not confirmed. Positions are guesses until recorded on site.
name: Church Street and the village hall

layers.essential_history: [[c:Church Street runs from the village crossroads to the church and the old manor, the oldest part of the village.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Nassington and its neighbour Yarwell share a long history along the River Nene.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Edith the cook stops you. She says the poet Orm was singing in the kitchen all night, and the bread ovens prove it.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:Edith's loaves]]
material: [[c:EDITH: "Orm sang one song for every batch of loaves. I baked from dusk to dawn: six batches, each taking two hours."]]
puzzle.question: [[c:How many hours did Orm sing for?]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:Twelve hours: Orm was singing in the kitchen all night.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]

evidence: [[c:Orm the poet sang in the kitchen all night.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Carry on along Church Street to the church, about 200 metres.]]
